$comment: Configuration of the API parity tests (src\WebAwesome.Blazor.Tests\ApiParity). 'enabled' and 'targetWaVersion' are set by the wa-upgrade process (Phase 3) once expected-api-surface.json matches the version being implemented.

Every other top-level member except 'components', 'ignoreReasons' and 'knownDefects' is an allowlist or override, and so is every member of a 'components' entry (semantics: the summaries in ApiParityModels.cs and docs\UPGRADE-PROCESS.md, Testing strategy).

Every entry needs a reason of its own, keyed '<list>:<tag>:<entry>' for a per-component list (e.g. 'ignoredEvents:wa-checkbox:change') or '<list>:<entry>' for a top-level one (e.g. 'globalIgnoredAttributes:title'); the entry is the list item or the map key. The reason goes into 'ignoreReasons' for a deliberate deviation, or into 'knownDefects' for a defect awaiting an owner decision - never both, and never a reason shared by name across components.

AllowlistHygieneTests fails on an entry without a reason, a reason without an entry, a KNOWN DEFECT marker inside 'ignoreReasons', and a change of the number of known defects (pinned in the test, printed in its output). Stale entries fail the *_AreNotStale test of the class reading the list.
extraElementMethods and sourceVerifiedEvents are invisible to the CEM diff: re-verify them against the target version's source on every upgrade.

ignoreReasons.extraRenderedAttributes:wa-page:disable-: wa-page's disable-sticky is a CSS-only attribute the CEM omits: the 3.12.0 page styles match it with :host([disable-sticky~='banner'|'header'|'subheader'|'aside'|'menu']) rules (chunk.NSKMM5IJ.js:86-116) and page.md (Sticky Sections) documents it; WaPage.DisableSticky renders the WaPageSections tokens, which FlagTokenTests pins - re-verify every upgrade
ignoreReasons.onOffAttributes:wa-input:autocorrect: wa-input's autocorrect converter is fromAttribute: (value) => !value || value === "off" ? false : true, toAttribute: value ? "on" : "off" (3.12.0 chunk.3UR7XKQK.js), so a present empty attribute (Blazor's true) reads false; AutoCorrect (bool?) must render exactly "on"/"off"
ignoreReasons.onOffAttributes:wa-textarea:autocorrect: wa-textarea's autocorrect has the same on/off converter as wa-input (3.12.0 chunk.YIEXWZ6G.js), so AutoCorrect must render exactly "on"/"off"
ignoreReasons.onOffAttributes:wa-combobox:autocorrect: wa-combobox's autocorrect has the same on/off converter as wa-input (3.12.0 chunk.HYTAIWXE.js), so AutoCorrect must render exactly "on"/"off"
ignoreReasons.tokenListAttributes:wa-zoomable-frame:sa: wa-zoomable-frame forwards sandbox to its iframe (sandbox=${ifDefined(this.sandbox)}, 3.12.0 chunk.PJARYDTD.js); the CEM types it string, but HTML defines it as a space-separated set of these tokens (HTML Living Standard, the iframe sandbox attribute), which WaIframeSandbox flags emit; re-verify every upgrade
ignoreReasons.tokenListAttributes:wa-zoomable-frame:re: wa-zoomable-frame forwards referrerpolicy to its iframe (3.12.0 chunk.PJARYDTD.js); the CEM types it string, but the value is one referrer-policy token of this fixed set (W3C Referrer Policy), which WaReferrerPolicy emits; the token check validates the single value
ignoreReasons.tokenListAttributes:wa-accordion:heading: wa-accordion's heading-level is typed string, but the element reads it as parseInt 1..6 (else 3) or "none" to omit the heading (3.12.0 chunk.LVL7ACR6.js renderHeadingWrapper and render); WaHeadingLevel emits exactly those tokens
ignoreReasons.wrapperDefaultAttributes:wa-checkbox:val: the submission value is the constant 'True', rendered always, like Blazor's InputCheckbox (see unrenderedAttributes:wa-checkbox:value); the element leaves value unset and submits 'on'
ignoreReasons.wrapperDefaultAttributes:wa-switch:value: the submission value is the constant 'True', rendered always, like Blazor's InputCheckbox (see unrenderedAttributes:wa-switch:value); the element leaves value unset and submits 'on'
ignoreReasons.wrapperDefaultAttributes:wa-slider:value: WaRange renders its two-way bound decimal value (0 when unbound) as value in single mode; the value of a bound control comes from the binding, not from an element default
ignoreReasons.divergentParameterDefaults:wa-slider:val: WaRange.Value is the two-way bound value of InputBase<decimal>, whose C# default is default(decimal), 0, like every non-nullable bound model; the element's default value is computed at runtime from min (or min-value), which the CEM cannot express
ignoreReasons.wrapperDefaultAttributes:wa-radio-group:: WaRadioGroup renders name from Blazor's InputBase form integration (the bound field's name, here the harness's ValueExpression field), so a bound control always carries a name
ignoreReasons.globalIgnoredAttributes:title: native HTML attribute, passed through via AdditionalAttributes
ignoreReasons.globalIgnoredAttributes:did-ssr: internal SSR hydration marker set by Web Awesome server-side rendering (added to every component's base element in WA 3.3.0); not a consumer-authorable attribute
ignoreReasons.globalIgnoredAttributes:dir: native HTML global attribute, passed through via AdditionalAttributes (added to every component's base element in WA 3.3.0)
ignoreReasons.globalIgnoredAttributes:lang: native HTML global attribute, passed through via AdditionalAttributes (added to every component's base element in WA 3.3.0)
ignoreReasons.globalIgnoredAttributes:role: native ARIA global HTML attribute; WA 3.8.0 reflects an internal default role onto the host of several components (wa-rating='slider', wa-tab='tab', wa-tab-panel='tabpanel', wa-tree='tree', wa-tree-item='treeitem') as part of its own accessibility management - not a consumer-authorable parameter, passed through via AdditionalAttributes when overridden
ignoreReasons.globalIgnoredAttributes:tabindex: native HTML global attribute; WA 3.8.0 reflects a managed tabindex onto wa-tree (0) and wa-tree-item (-1) to implement roving-tabindex keyboard navigation - not a consumer-authorable parameter, passed through via AdditionalAttributes when overridden
ignoreReasons.componentClassOverrides:wa-textarea: the CEM class name of wa-textarea is WaTextarea; the wrapper is named WaTextArea, the natural PascalCase of 'text area' used across .NET (TextArea)
ignoreReasons.nativeElementMethods:focus: HTMLElement.focus(), which every element inherits (so the CEM lists it for none); invoked by the wrappers' FocusAsync methods
ignoreReasons.nativeElementMethods:blur: HTMLElement.blur(), which every element inherits (so the CEM lists it for none); invoked by the wrappers' BlurAsync methods
ignoreReasons.nativeElementMethods:click: HTMLElement.click(), which every element inherits (so the CEM lists it for none); invoked by the wrappers' ClickAsync methods
ignoreReasons.nativeDomEvents:blur: native blur, dispatched by the browser on the focused element; Blazor delivers it (non-bubbling) only to composedPath()[0], so a wrapper binds it only where the host itself takes the focus (wa-radio, wa-tab, wa-dropdown-item), several of which do not list it in their CEM entry; controls focused inside their shadow root bind focusout instead (bubblingEventAliases)
ignoreReasons.nativeDomEvents:click: native click, dispatched by the browser on any element (composed, bubbling out of the shadow tree); Web Awesome documents no click event for wa-button, wa-tab or wa-breadcrumb-item because it is not theirs to dispatch
ignoreReasons.nativeDomEvents:focus: native focus, dispatched by the browser on the focused element; Blazor delivers it (non-bubbling) only to composedPath()[0], so a wrapper binds it only where the host itself takes the focus (wa-radio, wa-tab, wa-dropdown-item), several of which do not list it in their CEM entry; controls focused inside their shadow root bind focusin instead (bubblingEventAliases)
ignoreReasons.nativeDomEvents:keydown: native keyboard event, dispatched by the browser on the focused element and composed out of the shadow tree, so the host of every focusable form control receives it; Web Awesome documents no keyboard events. wa-select, wa-combobox and wa-color-picker stop its propagation in their shadow root, so the JS initializer relays it for them (relayedEvents, wablazor-keydown) and their wrappers bind the relayed name, which the binding checks resolve to keydown
ignoreReasons.nativeDomEvents:keypress: native keyboard event, dispatched by the browser on the focused element and composed out of the shadow tree, so the host of every focusable form control receives it; Web Awesome documents no keyboard events
ignoreReasons.nativeDomEvents:keyup: native keyboard event, dispatched by the browser on the focused element and composed out of the shadow tree, so the host of every focusable form control receives it; Web Awesome documents no keyboard events
ignoreReasons.bubblingEventAliases:focusin: OnFocus binds the bubbling, composed focusin wherever the focus can land inside the shadow root (every WaInputBase control, WaButton, WaFileInput): the element-level focus does not bubble, and Blazor delivers a non-bubbling event only to composedPath()[0], the inner input, so a focus handler on the host never ran. focusin reaches the host and bubbles on to Blazor, and a focus move between two parts of the same shadow root is not dispatched outside it; the checks treat a focusin handler as the element's focus
ignoreReasons.bubblingEventAliases:focusout: OnBlur binds the bubbling, composed focusout for the same reason as OnFocus binds focusin (see bubblingEventAliases:focusin); the checks treat a focusout handler as the element's blur
ignoreReasons.unreachableEnumUnionValues:WaChartLegend: 'center' comes from Chart.js' shared LayoutPosition type (a scale position); the Chart.js 4 legend documents only top, left, bottom, right and chartArea, so WaChartLegendPosition deliberately has no Center member
ignoreReasons.unreachableEnumUnionValues:WaSize: the long size spellings 'small'/'medium'/'large' are deprecated in WA 3.12.0 ('will be removed in the next major version'); WaSize.Small/Medium/Large emit the equivalent short forms 's'/'m'/'l' since 3.12.0, so the deprecated literals are intentionally unreachable
ignoreReasons.unreachableUnionValues:wa-badge:attentio: 'none' is the WA default (no animation); it is reached by leaving the nullable WaBadge.Attention unset, which omits the attribute, so WaAttention has no None member
ignoreReasons.eventOverrides:wa-details:wa-show: WaDetails raises OnToggle for both wa-show and wa-hide, with IsOpen telling them apart, like the native details toggle event, instead of separate OnShow/OnHide callbacks
ignoreReasons.eventOverrides:wa-details:wa-hide: WaDetails raises OnToggle for both wa-show and wa-hide, with IsOpen telling them apart, like the native details toggle event, instead of separate OnShow/OnHide callbacks
